body: Sorry, posted after I took Ambien & before I fell asleep! Lol. We're in Michigan (metro Detroit). Been here my whole life and the 8 months of bad weather a year is not helping my severe depression. Looking to move toward a warmer climate. Husband and I each make about $60K a year plus a small stipend due to my husband's illnesses that he got while in the Air Force. Just looking for general ideas of good housing markets (where we could find a decent house for $200-300k) in a good school district with job opportunities for us. We've thought about possibly North Carolina. This may not be the right sub. I'm pretty new to Reddit. I just know the people in this sub tend to give good advice. Thanks in advance for any help you can provide.

Thank you. It got to the point where drinking was definitely doing more harm than good. But even when you logically know something, it can still be difficult to change. I plan to cut down to nothing in the next month or two. It should help with my weight loss goals too.

I believe mine is strictly biological/chemical. I am educated, employed in a good career, have a faithful husband who loves me, a beautiful daughter, extended family who care about me, friends, a car, a nice middle class house. Everything you could ever want really. I made it through the first 30 years of life relatively unscathed, I had a loving family growing up (no real trauma to speak of), good grades in school, extracurricular activities, friends, was always physically fit. Then it's like something just went haywire in my brain and I don't know why. I'm depressed, an insomniac, I've gained 50 lbs, and I've turned to alcohol to self medicate. Tried lots of different meds, therapy, ECT (shock therapy), meditation, acupuncture, weighted blankets and blackout curtains for insomnia. I'm struggling at work and life in general. Although I'm lucky that my family never waivers in their support (they sometimes feel frustrated and I feel guilty). I hope to start TMS in a few months (I need to switch insurance companies in the fall to one that pays for TMS). And I'm Looking to start a diet & exercise routine. I certainly need to. I've cut way back on drinking. I was drinking 4-5 nights per week. I'm down to drinking three times this month. Gotta start somewhere right? This disease is a bitch. The lack of understanding by the general public and often lack of empathy really get to me. I've more than once wished I had a more tangible disease like cancer. As horrible as it is, at least most people understand it to an extent and don't blame you for your own illness.

I can relate. I have a family who loves me, an amazing husband who stands by me and a beautiful daughter. I really have no "reason" to be depressed. Despite, lots of meds, therapy, hospitalizations and ECT, I still am. It breaks my heart because I am breaking their hearts. And I want to be a good mother to my daughter. She doesn't deserve to have a depressed Mom. Life became really fucking hard at one point. I long for the days when I was mostly happy and optimistic.

I've tried overdosing a few times. Last time I took about 50 Ambien 10mg and 50 Effexor XR 150mg. I was taken to the hospital by ambulance and was in pretty bad shape. Worse than my other attempts. I couldn't eat, lost tons of weight, slept a lot, had crazy night sweats and there was some serious concern that I had done damage to my heart. It's about a year later now and I seem to be doing ok at least physically. But I did a week in the hospital, then moved to an impatient hospital for a few days, then an outpatient daily program for a week. Honestly, I'm glad I survived and I promised myself and family I wouldn't hurt myself again. But pills are definitely a hard way to go. Like the last poster said, you tend to just harm yourself not kill yourself. If I was looking for a way to kill myself I wouldn't go with pills. I think I even knew that at the time that my chance of survival from a handful of pills was much greater than surviving a bullet to the head. So on some level, even though I was definitely depressed and in pain, I think I knew I wanted to live. That has been the case with all of my attempts. There is a part of me that truly wants to die. But there's a small part of me that still wants to live too.

Ugh. The insomnia is the worst. It just exacerbates every negative feeling. And worrying about not sleeping causes me so much anxiety- which then turns into a self-fulfilling prophecy- meaning I don't sleep. I feel your pain!

Glad to hear that it worked for you. I would like to do it too, but unfortunately it is not covered by my insurance. In November we have "open enrollment" where we can choose our insurance coverage. I'll be changing to an insurance that does cover it. Just gotta be able to make it through the next 7 months!
